# 1 Samuel Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 188 | **Source Image:** 1SA_011_page_001.jpg, 1SA_011_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And Nahash the Ammonite went up and encamped against Jabesh-gilead. And all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you."

**2** And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, "On this condition I will make a covenant with you: by gouging out every right eye among you, and I will set it as a reproach upon all Israel."

**3** And the elders of Jabesh said to him, "Give us seven days, that we may send messengers throughout all the territory of Israel. And if there is no one to save us, then we will come out to you."

**4** And the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the ears of the people, and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.

**5** And behold, Saul was coming in from the field behind the oxen. And Saul said, "What is the matter with the people, that they weep?" And they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.

**6** And the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned fiercely.

**7** And he took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen!" And the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.

**8** And he mustered them at Bezek, and the sons of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

**9** And they said to the messengers who had come, "Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have deliverance.'" And the messengers went and told the men of Jabesh, and they were glad.

**10** And the men of Jabesh said, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever is good in your eyes."

**11** And it came to pass on the next day that Saul set the people in three companies, and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck the Ammonites until the heat of the day. And those who remained were so scattered that no two of them were left together.

**12** And the people said to Samuel, "Who is the one who said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Give us the men, and we will put them to death."

**13** And Saul said, "No man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked deliverance in Israel."

**14** And Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there."

**15** And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. And they sacrificed there peace offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced there greatly.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes
All three translators agreed in substance on the core narrative structure and meaning of this chapter. The sequence of events — Nahash's threat, Jabesh's plea, Saul's Spirit-empowered response, the military victory, and the renewal of kingship at Gilgal — was rendered consistently across all three versions. Verses 4, 8, 9, 12, and 14 showed strong convergence in wording.

---
## Disagreement Log

**Verse 1** — *"covenant" vs. "treaty"*
- EMET: "Cut for us a covenant" (hyper-literal, retaining Hebrew idiom)
- LOGOS: "Make a covenant with us"
- PNEUMA: "Make a treaty with us"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "covenant" (LOGOS), as *berit* is a theologically loaded term in the Hebrew Bible and "treaty" flattens the covenantal resonance.

**Verse 2** — *"reproach" vs. "disgrace"*
- EMET: "I will set it as a reproach upon all Israel"
- LOGOS: "I will set it as a reproach upon all Israel"
- PNEUMA: "bring disgrace on all Israel"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "reproach" (EMET/LOGOS), which more precisely renders Hebrew *cherpah* and preserves the formal register.

**Verse 3** — *"saving us" vs. "comes to rescue us" / "come out to you" vs. "surrender to you"*
- EMET: "if there is no one saving us, then we will come out to you"
- LOGOS: "if there is no one saving us, then we will come out to you"
- PNEUMA: "If no one comes to rescue us, we will surrender to you"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "no one to save us" (formal baseline) and "come out to you" (EMET/LOGOS), preserving the Hebrew's ambiguity — "come out" could mean surrender or simply emerge from the city.

**Verse 4** — *"spoke the words in the ears of the people" vs. "reported the terms to the people"*
- EMET: "they spoke the words in the ears of the people"
- LOGOS: "spoke the words in the ears of the people"
- PNEUMA: "reported the terms to the people"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "spoke the words in the ears of the people" (EMET/LOGOS), preserving the Hebrew idiom.

**Verse 5** — *"What is wrong with the people that they weep?" vs. "What is the matter with the people?"*
- EMET: "What is wrong with the people that they weep?"
- LOGOS: "What is the matter with the people, that they weep?"
- PNEUMA: "What is wrong with the people? Why are they crying?"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "What is the matter with the people, that they weep?" (LOGOS) for natural English with formal register.

**Verse 6** — *"exceedingly" vs. "greatly" vs. "fiercely"*
- EMET: "his anger burned exceedingly"
- LOGOS: "his anger burned greatly"
- PNEUMA: "he burned with fierce anger"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "his anger burned fiercely," combining the formal structure of EMET/LOGOS with PNEUMA's stronger adverb that better conveys the Hebrew *me'od* in context of divine empowerment.

**Verse 7** — *"dread of YHWH" vs. "dread of the LORD" vs. "God-sent terror"*
- EMET: "dread of YHWH"
- LOGOS: "dread of the LORD"
- PNEUMA: "A God-sent terror"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "dread of the LORD" (LOGOS), the standard English rendering of the divine name in formal translation.

**Verse 10** — *"according to all the good in your eyes" vs. "whatever you see fit"*
- EMET: "according to all the good in your eyes"
- LOGOS: "all that is good in your eyes"
- PNEUMA: "whatever you see fit"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "whatever is good in your eyes" — a slight smoothing of the formal rendering while preserving the Hebrew idiom.

**Verse 11** — *"put the people in three companies" vs. "organized his forces into three divisions"*
- EMET: "Saul put the people in three companies"
- LOGOS: "Saul set the people in three companies"
- PNEUMA: "Saul organized his forces into three divisions"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "Saul set the people in three companies" (LOGOS), retaining the Hebrew term structure.

**Verse 13** — *"has made deliverance" vs. "has worked deliverance" vs. "has accomplished a great deliverance"*
- EMET: "YHWH has made deliverance in Israel"
- LOGOS: "the LORD has worked deliverance in Israel"
- PNEUMA: "the LORD has accomplished a great deliverance in Israel"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "the LORD has worked deliverance in Israel" (LOGOS). PNEUMA adds "great" which is not in the Hebrew of this verse.

**Verse 14** — *"renew" vs. "reaffirm"*
- EMET: "let us renew there the kingship"
- LOGOS: "renew the kingship there"
- PNEUMA: "reaffirm the kingship"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Used "renew" (EMET/LOGOS), which directly translates Hebrew *chadash*.

**Verse 15** — *"peace offerings" vs. "fellowship sacrifices"*
- EMET: "sacrifices of peace offerings"
- LOGOS: "sacrifices of peace offerings"
- PNEUMA: "fellowship sacrifices"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "peace offerings" (EMET/LOGOS), the traditional rendering of *shelamim*.
